utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You may sit down. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-13/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic, Miroslav Radic and Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you. Mr. Mrksic, could you follow the proceedings in your own language? THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If at any time until we finish this status conference you have problems with interpretation, please draw my attention to that immediately. And I am telling you this at the same time I am passing on the same message to the other two accused. Okay. You may sit down. Thank you. Mr. Radic, the same question to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language? THE ACCUSED RADIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Sljivancanin, can you follow the proceedings in your own language? THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone. I can follow the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I welcome you all to this status conference, which is convened while proceedings under Rule 11 bis are ongoing, pending. So it will be more or less a shortened status conference, for all intents and purposes. May I ask for presentations. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning -- good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. Also good afternoon to the Defence. I'm here together with co-counsel Ms. Marie Tuma and our case manager, Lise-Lotte Karlsson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to your team. Appearances for Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to my colleagues. Appearing for Mr. Mile Mrksic, Miroslav Vasic, attorney at law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you. Appearances for Miroslav Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Attorney Borivoje Borovic will be appearing today for Mr. Miroslav Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Borovic. And appearances for Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. My name is Novak Lukic, Defence counsel for Mr. Veselin Sljivancanin, accompanied today by Mr. Momcilo Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic and good morning to you both. I apologise to all of you if we are meeting in this small courtroom, which is usually avoided when you have more than one accused, but we had no alternatives. As you know, the -- at the present, the Tribunal is operating at full steam and sometimes it's difficult to find courtrooms available. So I also accepted to do this in this courtroom precisely because I know that this is going to be a fairly short status conference. However, I hope you will not feel inconvenienced because of this. You will recall that the last status conference in this case was convened on the 4th of February 2005, and a lot of water has passed under the bridges since then and 11 bis proceedings have been commenced, as you are aware. Still, the existence of 11 bis proceedings do not lift the obligation that the Trial Chamber has of -- and the Pre-Trial Judge has of convening Pre-Trial status conference on a regular basis as required by the Rules. And that means within 120 days from the previous status conference, which is the case today. This is being convened within that time limit. For the benefit of the public in particular, I will just point out that the purpose of these periodical status conferences is first, to organise exchanges between the parties with a view to ensuring an expeditious preparation for the trial; secondly, to review the status of the accused's case and to allow the accused -- give each of the accused an opportunity to raise issues related thereto; and last but certainly not least, to give an opportunity to each of the accused to raise issues related to their mental and physical conditions as well as matters related to detention. As I said, that given that there are Rule 11 bis proceedings pending, the consequence is that some of the issues that are normally dealt with at length during status conferences will not be -- will not need to be dealt with at such length today. Let me just say for the time being that there are no outstanding motions in this case to my knowledge, and that since the last status conference, the Trial Chamber has handed down several decisions. Usually I adopt the approach of mentioning these decisions because I think it's the best opportunity that there is for the public to know what the Trial Chamber has been doing during these 120 days. There was a motion by accused Sljivancanin which was filed way back in December of last year, and this motion related to a challenge that he was making to the form of the indictment. On the 9th of March, we granted the Prosecution's submission and ordered that the third modified consolidated amended indictment filed by the Prosecution on the 16th of November 2004 would be and was going to be the operative indictment in this case. On the same day, on the 9th of March 2005, we also handed down a decision related to two Prosecution motions on protective measures that had been filed earlier on, particularly on the 17th of December of 2004 and 31st of January of 2005 respectively. As I said on the 9th of March of this year, in our decision, we ordered that the Pre-Trial protective measures of a pseudonym and non-disclosure of identity until 30 days prior to the start of trial be granted and maintained for five sensitive witnesses. We also granted protective measures during trial proceedings for 15 witnesses, while we denied the Prosecution request in regard to two witnesses, with the caveat, with the understanding, the proviso, that the Prosecution was being given the possibility to provide additional information concerning real risks to the security of these two witnesses and/or of their families, their respective families. And of course, therefore, in regard to these two persons, the position of the Trial Chamber is reserved. In the meantime, there are no protective measures granted. Then, earlier on, precisely on the 10th of February of this year, we dealt with confidential and ex parte request by accused Radic for review of the decision by Registrar on the remuneration of counsel. This had been filed on the 31st of December of 2004. On the 10th of February 2005, we denied the request, and held that the Registry had not impeded in any way or interfered with the fairness of the trial in reaching its decision on remuneration of counsel, to which counsel had found objection. On the 3rd of March 2005, we dealt with a related sort of request from the Defence, which had been filed on the 27th of January 2005. This request was for review of the Registrar's decision on the level of the case. On the 3rd of March 2005, as I said, we denied this request and held that the Registry had not in any way impeded the fairness of the trial in deciding that the case was of level 1 complexity. There was then a request by accused Mrksic relating to provisional release. This was filed on the 23rd of February 2005. Basically on the 9th of March 2005, we denied the accused's motion for provisional release on the basis that we were not satisfied that if provisionally released accused Mrksic would appear for trial and that he will not pose a danger to any victim-witness or any other person. In addition, we also held that the length of his pre-trial detention, in the present case, was proportional to the circumstances and complexity of the case, as brought against him in the indictment. I also need to mention that on the 19th of April of this year, the Appeals Chamber denied accused Mrksic leave to appeal on the basis -- to appeal this Trial Chamber's decision, on the basis that he had failed to demonstrate how the Trial Chamber - that's us, me and my two colleagues, Judge Antonetti and Judge Parker - had erred in taking or reaching that decision that I mentioned earlier and which goes back to the 9th of March. So more or less, this is a report on the activities of the Trial Chamber in response to motions that have been forthcoming. And as I said, to my knowledge, there are no outstanding motions, at least before the Pre-Trial Chamber. Which leads me on to the next part of the agenda, that is matters related to disclosure. And I would first refer to disclosure required under our rules and under -- pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii). I refer you back to what was stated on the 20th of January of this year by the Prosecution. I can't confirm necessarily that it was Mr. Wubben but I think it was Mr. Wubben. We were told on the 20th of January that the Prosecution had submitted an updated witness list pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii). What I'm interested in knowing is whether this witness list stands or whether it has been altered or whether we are to expect any amendments to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Are there any comments from anyone of the Defence counsel on this? I see none. I see none. So we proceed to disclosure of oral statements to the Defence. Again, during the previous status conference, the February one, I pointed out that it was apparent that out of the 48 witness statements disclosed by the Prosecution, that is practically all the witnesses with the exception of those five witnesses for which delayed disclosure of identity pursuant to Rule 69 had been requested and was actually granted later on, the B/C/S version of 11 statements had not yet been provided. In addition, also, during the last status conference, the Defence submitted that as regards two statements, neither the B/C/S nor the English version had been provided. You will recall that I was not happy with that situation, and that as a result I had imposed the 15th of March of 2005 as a clear deadline for the Prosecution to make these translations available to the Defence, to the accused and to the Defence. So I look to my right and I would like to have a confirmation if at all from the three Defence representatives as to whether you are happy now that all due translations have been handed or delivered to you. Yes, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As regards these statements, on the 11th of March 2005, our Defence team received nine out of 11 such statements in B/C/S and with regard to two witnesses, we received confirmation from the Prosecution that they do not have their statements either in English or in B/C/S. With that confirmation, the Defence believes that the obligations of the Prosecution have been honoured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Borovic, do you agree with Mr. Vasic or do you want to make a different submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we agree on all counts. I would only add that the issue of transcripts and statements of these two witnesses are statements of witnesses who would be under 92 bis. These transcripts do not indicate that since we did not have a 65 ter conference we have not discussed this issue with regard to witnesses, and the Prosecution owes us a response, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. As soon as I finish with Mr. Lukic, I will of course address this matter to Mr. Wubben and if we need to discuss it we will discuss it here. Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to add to what my colleagues have already said. I subscribe to their statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Wubben, do you wish to add anything to what has been stated on this matter, in particular to what was raised by Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with a view to 92 bis, that's something for the future to decide within the strategy of the Prosecution, but my learned friend is right, we didn't had a 65 ter meeting, nor the opportunity to meet in advance to the status conference. So the Prosecution prefer to meet with counsel in that respect and exchange the relevant information. And so far, we believe we met the disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Wubben. And what's the situation as regards disclosure obligations under Rule 68? On my part, I would just like to remind everyone that according to my records, the Prosecution filed their latest partially confidential Prosecution fourth report concerning disclosure way back on the 9th of August 2004. Quite a long time ago, I would say. Detailing the material disclosed pursuant to Rule 68 to the three accused. Over time, the parties have been encouraged to cooperate as much as possible with each other on this issue, without, however, losing sight of the fact that the obligation under Rule 68, and for that matter also under Rule 66(A)(ii) as the case may be, lies on the Prosecution. Are there any developments in this area?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for triggering the disclosure-report issue because a good practice should be that from time to time we confirm to parties to agree upon a past disclosure. We did new ISU search in this case, meaning that we have lots of documents to disclose. We already reviewed it and there will be disclosure. We planned it this week so the first part of it will be disclosed under Rule 68 tomorrow in I guess three parts. That's one issue I would like to inform you about. We already disclosed prior, lots of documents concerning the trial in Belgrade, and my learned friends are updated of the fact that we did so in two batches also, including those Rule 68, meaning that we first want to finalise these three batches in total and then we can confirm by our disclosure report and continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Are there any comments? Yes, Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are extremely happen which why the cooperation we have with the Office of the Prosecutor, the cooperation that we've had since the last status conference in particular. I would only add that the material disclosed after the last status conference is a great amount of material, namely statements delivered by the district court in Belgrade. They are in B/C/S. It is not indicated, however, under what rule these statements fall. I would appreciate an answer from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Wubben, do I take it that all the Belgrade trial material is going to be disclosed under Rule 68 or only part of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are nearly disclosing everything. Well, when it comes to an arrest warrant or an administrative notification, as it turned out to be, then no disclosure is needed. But as long as it is relevant, any lawyer might say as a whole it includes a Rule 68. But it's better to have an arrangement by parties and we did so last year. The request towards the Office of the Prosecutor is if possible, if you are in a position to disclose it, please disclose to us as soon as possible and don't mind about Rule 68 or whatever it is for us relevant to know as soon as possible and that we can work out also with a view to our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any further comments, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Firstly on this issue, I was one of those who were pushing for more disclosure, and as we get material from the Prosecution we will be able to ask for clarification later. And I have to compliment the Prosecution with regard to material delivered from Belgrade. It seems there are something like 3.000 pages of transcript, which is in many ways crucial for our case, but what is reason for particular satisfaction in our eyes is that we were immediately given B/C/S materials, and I would appreciate very much if we could get English versions as soon as possible so that the Prosecution can familiarise themselves with this material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So I had in mind or planned to raise the matter of the Belgrade trial, the Ovcara farm proceedings, myself. But I don't think there is anything else that I need to add on this matter. I think we have been provided with all the information. Which brings me to the next part of the agenda, namely agreed facts. Usually we go into detail as may be required but in the circumstances of the current 11 bis proceedings, I don't think we need to waste time on this. If there is an interest between the parties of proceeding along the path of agreed facts, please do so by all means, and we will deal with those later on. I mean the 11 bis proceedings are pending but it doesn't mean to say that they will definitely be decided granting a referral. Are there any other matters you would like to raise? Let's start with you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will address you on behalf of all three Defence teams. We have nothing to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So -- but I need to hear each and every one of your clients. Mr. Mrksic, you'll recall that at the end of the status conference I always put some questions to you in relation to your state of health and your state of detention. Would you like to tell me something about these two matters or is everything -- THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is in good order and I have nothing to add to what was said last time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Radic, the same question to you. THE ACCUSED RADIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I also have nothing to add and everything is in good order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Sljivancanin, the same question to you. THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I abide by everything I have said to died and I have nothing new to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. That basically brings us to the end of there status conference, unless you can think of any other business to transact. I don't think there is anything else that needs to be discussed. So we stand adjourned. And the next status conference will be convened within 120 days from today, if the case is still before this Tribunal. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
